_about: Hand-curated investment candidates for the Investments tab. Speculation: theses come from how these items went in WoW Classic and from player progression, not from Forever data. Prices, trends and 'used in' recipes shown next to them are Forever data. Checked against the item database on 2026-11-13; an id whose name no longer matches is dropped and listed on the tab.

items.name: Black Lotus
items.thesis: Every flask needs one, and flasks are raid staples. In Classic it stayed one of the most valuable materials for the whole game because spawns are few and contested.
items.risk_note: Already expensive; slow to sell (low sale rate).

items.name: Dreamfoil
items.thesis: Goes into flasks (30 each), protection potions and many endgame elixirs. In Classic demand grew steadily with raiding.
items.risk_note: Herbalists at 60 add a lot of supply.

items.name: Mountain Silversage
items.thesis: Used in Elixir of the Mongoose and flasks: core raid consumables in Classic.
items.risk_note: Common herb; supply grows with herbalists at 60.

items.name: Plaguebloom
items.thesis: Used in Elixir of the Mongoose and other endgame elixirs. In Classic it was one of the pricier endgame herbs because it grows mostly in Felwood and the Plaguelands.
items.risk_note: Price depends on few elixir recipes being widely known.

items.name: Icecap
items.thesis: Few uses, but two of them are flasks. In Classic its price jumped whenever raiders bought flasks, and it grows only in Winterspring.
items.risk_note: Very slow seller now (low sale rate): you may wait a long time.

items.name: Gromsblood
items.thesis: Flask of the Titans needs 30. In Classic tanks' flasks kept it in demand.
items.risk_note: Mostly flask demand; other uses are minor.

items.name: Golden Sansam
items.thesis: Main herb in Major Healing Potions, which every raider uses.
items.risk_note: Cheapest of the endgame herbs: lots of supply.

items.name: Major Healing Potion
items.thesis: Every raider drinks them. In Classic potion prices followed raid nights and herb prices.
items.risk_note: Price is capped by herb cost plus a small margin, since many alchemists can make it.

items.name: Major Mana Potion
items.thesis: Healers and casters use them every raid; steady demand in Classic.
items.risk_note: Capped by herb cost, like healing potions.

items.name: Greater Fire Protection Potion
items.thesis: In Classic it sold out before guilds learned Molten Core and Ragnaros, then settled once fire resistance gear replaced it.
items.risk_note: Almost no sales now; only worth holding if a fire raid is coming.

items.name: Elixir of the Mongoose
items.thesis: The melee raid elixir. In Classic the recipe was a rare drop, so few alchemists could make it and the price held.
items.risk_note: Slow seller now; depends on how rare the recipe is in Forever.

items.name: Elemental Fire
items.thesis: Fire protection potions and fire resistance crafts. In Classic demand rose with Molten Core and Onyxia.
items.risk_note: Farmed easily from fire elementals; supply can keep up.

items.name: Elemental Earth
items.thesis: Elemental Sharpening Stones (a melee raid consumable) and many crafts; steady seller in Classic.
items.risk_note: Cheap and plentiful; upside is modest.

items.name: Elemental Water
items.thesis: Frost protection potions and frost resistance crafts, which matter for later raids.
items.risk_note: Demand may come only with later content.

items.name: Elemental Air
items.thesis: Used in many leatherworking and engineering crafts; fewer sources than other elementals.
items.risk_note: Lower sale rate than Earth or Fire.

items.name: Essence of Fire
items.thesis: Endgame crafts and alchemy transmutes. In Classic essence prices rose as crafters reached 300 skill.
items.risk_note: Alchemists can transmute essences into each other, which caps the price gaps.

items.name: Essence of Earth
items.thesis: Endgame crafts and transmutes, like Essence of Fire.
items.risk_note: Transmutes link its price to the other essences.

items.name: Essence of Water
items.thesis: Used in the most recipes of the four essences (Forever's recipe table lists them).
items.risk_note: Already the priciest essence; transmutes cap it.

items.name: Essence of Air
items.thesis: The rarest essence; in Classic it was often the most expensive one.
items.risk_note: Very few sales now: the listed price may be wishful.

items.name: Essence of Undeath
items.thesis: Endgame tailoring bags and weapon crafts; dropped by undead in the Plaguelands and Scholomance.
items.risk_note: Supply rises as players farm the Plaguelands.

items.name: Arcane Crystal
items.thesis: Needed for Transmute: Arcanite. In Classic it stayed valuable because only rich Thorium veins drop it.
items.risk_note: Its price follows Arcanite, which fell in Classic as more alchemists could transmute.

items.name: Thorium Bar
items.thesis: Used in over 100 recipes, including the Arcanite transmute; high volume and quick to sell.
items.risk_note: Miners at 60 add a lot of supply; small upside.

items.name: Arcanite Bar
items.thesis: Epic crafted weapons and armor need it. In Classic it was most expensive early, while few alchemists had the daily transmute.
items.risk_note: Classic's pattern is a fall over time: more likely a sell-now item than one to hold.

items.name: Large Brilliant Shard
items.thesis: In Classic the Crusader enchant and most endgame enchants used it, and its price followed raid enchanting demand.
items.risk_note: Every disenchanted endgame blue adds supply.

items.name: Greater Eternal Essence
items.thesis: Endgame enchants for raid gear.
items.risk_note: Supply grows with dungeon runs.

items.name: Illusion Dust
items.thesis: The dust for most endgame enchants; demand grows as raiders enchant their gear.
items.risk_note: Plentiful from disenchanting endgame greens.

items.name: Righteous Orb
items.thesis: In Classic the Crusader enchant needed it and it dropped mainly in Stratholme, so it stayed one of the pricier enchanting materials.
items.risk_note: Already expensive; supply grows with Stratholme runs.

items.name: Runecloth
items.thesis: Bandages, tailoring (as Bolts of Runecloth) and reputation turn-ins. In Classic it was priciest in the first months, then fell as more players farmed at 50-60.
items.risk_note: Classic's pattern is a fall: hold only short term.

items.name: Felcloth
items.thesis: Tailors turn it into Mooncloth, and warlocks want Felcloth bags. Drops from few mobs.
items.risk_note: Price follows Mooncloth demand.

items.name: Mooncloth
items.thesis: Made once per cooldown per tailor, so supply is limited; used in many endgame robes and bags.
items.risk_note: Very slow seller now.

items.name: Devilsaur Leather
items.thesis: Devilsaur gauntlets and leggings were pre-raid best-in-slot for hunters and rogues. In Classic prices were highest when players first reached 60, then fell as raid gear replaced them.
items.risk_note: A rise-then-fall item: sell into the peak, don't hold it long.

items.name: Rugged Leather
items.thesis: Used in over 200 recipes, including armor kits; high volume.
items.risk_note: Skinners at 60 add a lot of supply; small upside.

items.name: Raw Nightfin Snapper
items.thesis: Cooks into Nightfin Soup, a mana food for healers. In Classic it could only be caught at night, which limits supply.
items.risk_note: Fishers can keep up if demand is modest.

items.name: Raw Winter Squid
items.thesis: Only caught in winter (Forever catches confirm it's winter now). Grilled Squid (+10 Agility) is raid food, so it should be worth more in summer when nobody can catch it.
items.risk_note: Spoils nothing, but lots of it is being caught now: buy only near the end of winter.
